title: First Steps Using a Jupyter Notebook
author: Alise J Ponsero
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6uphevn

steps.title: Download and install Anaconda
steps.instruction: Open a web browser, go to https://www.anaconda.com/distribution/, and download the installer for your operating system (Windows, MacOS, or Linux). For Windows, run the executable and follow the installation wizard using the recommended settings, then open Anaconda Navigator via the desktop menu search bar. For MacOS, run the downloaded package, follow the recommended settings, and find Anaconda Navigator in the Applications folder.

steps.title: Create a new conda environment
steps.instruction: Launch Anaconda Navigator, click the "Environments" sidebar, then press the "Create" button (lower left). Name the environment "class_2019" and select Python 3.7 in the popup, then click the green "Create" button and wait a few minutes for default packages to install.

steps.title: Install Biopython in the environment
steps.instruction: With the "class_2019" environment selected, change the package filter to "Not installed", type "Biopython" in the search bar, select the package, click the green "Apply" button, confirm the list of installations in the popup, click "Apply" again, then clear the search bar and verify that Biopython appears in the "Installed" view.

steps.title: Install and launch Jupyter Notebook
steps.instruction: Ensure the environment selector at the top of the Home tab is set to "class_2019", locate the Jupyter Notebook tile and click "Install" (wait for completion). After installation, click the "Launch" button, which starts a Jupyter server in your web browser. Navigate to your Documents directory, click "New" → "Python3" to create your first notebook.

steps.title: Troubleshoot Jupyter launch
steps.instruction: If the launch button does not open anything, try the following fixes in order: (1) Open a browser and go to http://localhost:8888/tree. (2) In Anaconda Navigator’s Environments tab, click the green arrow next to "class_2019" and choose "Open with Jupyter Notebook". (3) In the Home tab, with "class_2019" selected, install the "Jupyter Lab" tile, then launch Jupyter Lab, navigate to Documents, and create a notebook via the "Notebook Python3" tile.

steps.title: Verify notebook functionality
steps.instruction: In the first notebook cell type: print("Hello world") and run it with Shift+Enter; the output should be Hello world. In a second cell type: import Bio and run with Shift+Enter; there should be no output. If both work, rename the notebook via the File → Rename menu (interface should be in English).

steps.title: Re‑install Biopython in base environment if needed
steps.instruction: If importing Bio fails, open Anaconda Navigator, go to the Environments tab, select the "base" environment, repeat the Biopython installation steps (search, apply), then open a Jupyter notebook again and try "import Bio".

steps.title: Shut down the Jupyter server
steps.instruction: In the notebook window, click the "LogOut" button at the top right (or, in Jupyter Lab, choose File → Shutdown). A message should confirm that the server was turned off properly.
